title: Rhubarb pie, double-crust
subtitle: Sharp and sweet, rhubarb under a buttery pastry lid
excerpt: Rhubarb pie is one of the sharpest-fruited pies in the British and American canon, sweetened with plenty of sugar to balance the intense acidity of the stalks. A double shortcrust crust, base and lid, contains a filling that bubbles and thickens during baking. Serve warm with thick cream.
sourceNotes: Rhubarb pie appears in British recipe collections from the 19th century. Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136, documents rhubarb tarts with sugar. The double-crust format is the standard American approach, documented in early 20th century American home-baking literature.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked and cooled. Wrap tightly. Defrost overnight and warm at 170°C for 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry can be made 2 days ahead. The filling can sit, mixed, in the fridge for 1 day before baking.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional oven for first 20 minutes to set the lid; drop to 180°C for final 30 minutes; fan 180°C then 160°C

glossaryTerms.definition: Rhubarb grown in darkness in sheds, available from January. Paler pink, more tender, and less sharp than outdoor rhubarb. Both types work in this pie; forced rhubarb needs a little less sugar.

content.text: Rhubarb pie is intensely sharp and deeply comforting. The key is using enough sugar to tame the rhubarb without muting it, and enough cornflour to bind the plentiful juice so the filling does not flood out of the pie when cut. Use
in winter and spring; outdoor rhubarb from May onwards.

attrs.prepNote: trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Rub 200 g cold butter into 400 g flour, 30 g sugar, and a pinch of salt until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add 5 to 6 tablespoons cold water and bring together to a dough. Divide two thirds / one third (base and lid). Wrap both and chill for 30 minutes.

Toss the rhubarb with 250 g caster sugar, 40 g cornflour, the lemon juice and zest, and the vanilla. Let it sit for 15 minutes; the sugar draws juice from the rhubarb. The cornflour will thicken this juice during baking.

Roll the larger piece of pastry to 4 mm and line a 23 cm pie dish, leaving a 2 cm overhang. Pour in the filling. Roll the remaining pastry to a circle and lay over the filling. Press the overhang up and crimp the edges. Cut three or four vents in the lid. Brush with beaten egg and dust with a little sugar.

Bake at 200°C (conventional) for 20 minutes to set the lid. Drop the temperature to 180°C and bake for a further 30 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles through the vents. Rest for at least 30 minutes before cutting, the filling is very hot and liquid when it comes out of the oven.
